Job Description:

Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms, the Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation leads the architecture for Sun Life’s Intelligent Automation platforms.

The Director defines the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain strategy, future-state architectures, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps. The scope includes RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business process automation.

Working with business leaders, Technology Executives, other Enterprise Architects, application development teams, AI platform teams, security, privacy, operations, and engineering groups, the Director aligns Intelligent Automation investments and architecture decisions with business priorities, regulatory obligations, operational requirements, and measurable outcomes.

What will you do?

Define and maintain the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain architecture strategy, principles, standards, and technology roadmaps.
Assess the current-state RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture to identify capability gaps, risks, redundant technologies, technical debt, and opportunities for consolidation or modernization.
Define future-state architectures for RPA, intelligent document workflows, low-code automation, process mining, workflow orchestration, AI-assisted operations, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business processes.
Establish architecture patterns, guardrails, decision frameworks, and reference architectures that enable secure, scalable, resilient, auditable, and production-ready Intelligent Automation capabilities.
Collaborate with business leaders and Technology Executives to communicate architecture direction, options, trade-offs, investment considerations, risks, and expected outcomes for RPA and Intelligent Automation.
Drive platform standardization, reusable automation patterns, and approved citizen and professional development approaches to reduce duplication and improve delivery efficiency.
Collaborate with Enterprise, Domain, Solution, Application, Data, Cloud, Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, and AI Platform Architects to align automation decisions and resolve cross-domain dependencies.
Lead RPA and Intelligent Automation domain architecture governance, including architecture reviews, risk assessments, exception management, and architecture decision records, ensuring alignment with security, privacy, responsible AI, resilience, operational, regulatory, and compliance requirements.

What you’ll need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
Relevant certifications in RPA, Microsoft Power Platform, workflow automation, process mining, AI, security, or related technologies are considered assets.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, domain, portfolio, application, or platform architecture responsibility.
Significant experience designing, governing, and modernizing enterprise RPA, Intelligent Automation, workflow, or business process technology platforms.
Deep expertise in at least one major Intelligent Automation capability and broad knowledge across RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, Generative AI, and Agentic AI integration patterns.
Demonstrated experience defining RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture strategies, future-state architectures, technology roadmaps, standards, reference architectures, and governance practices.
Proven ability to collaborate with Technology Executives and influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, architecture options, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations.
Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture direction.
Knowledge of AI governance, AI risk management, responsible AI principles, privacy requirements, and enterprise AI adoption patterns as they apply to Intelligent Automation.
Ability to assess automation requirements and determine the appropriate platform, integration pattern, architecture approach, governance controls, and delivery boundaries.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including investment prioritization, value realization, platform rationalization, technical debt, risk, and technology portfolio trade-offs.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
Working together, sharing common values, and encouraging growth & achievement.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As Senior Director, Group Product Owner – Enterprise Governance, Risk & Compliance (eGRC), you'll shape how CIBC identifies, manages, and responds to operational risk. You will shift our programs from manual, periodic, judgment-based activities to connected, AI-enabled capabilities that anticipate risk, automate routine work, and focus people on the decisions that matter most.

You will lead CIBC's eGRC ecosystem, including the Operational Risk System (ORS) and enterprise operational risk data governance. With a mandate to rethink, not simply maintain, you'll define the target operating model, investment priorities, and product roadmap; simplify and automate risk work with our program team; and use connected data, advanced analytics, generative and agentic AI, and continuous monitoring to surface emerging risk and improve decisions. You will ensure these capabilities are deployed responsibly through strong data, model, security, privacy, control, and human-in-the-loop practices.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Enterprise Strategy and Transformation - Define the ambition, target operating model, and multi-year roadmap for CIBC's eGRC ecosystem. Align partners and investment to the highest risk and regulatory priorities, making bold, evidence-based choices that create lasting value.
Enterprise Product Leadership - Set priorities from discovery through adoption and continuous improvement. Establish disciplined governance, translate strategy into a clear roadmap, and use customer, risk, operational, and financial insight to accelerate outcomes and demonstrate value.
Reimagining Operational Risk Programs - Redesign core programs, including risk and control assessments, control management, issues, incidents, losses, scenarios, regulatory change, and reporting. Replace fragmented manual processes with simpler, automated, connected experiences that improve coverage, reduce administration, and focus attention on the highest-risk exposures and actions.
AI, Automation and Insight-Driven Risk - Make operational risk data a trusted enterprise asset across eGRC and ORS. Oversee the eGRC helpdesk to maintain responsive support and turn recurring pain points into improvements.

You're technically fluent and future-focused. You engage credibly with engineering, architecture, data, automation, design, security, and risk teams; understand platforms, integrations, analytics, generative and agentic AI, and responsible AI controls; and scale promising use cases into governed enterprise capabilities.
You turn ambiguity into momentum by framing problems, testing hypotheses, learning quickly, and adapting as user needs, technology, risk, and regulatory expectations evolve—without losing sight of the long-term ambition.
You're an inspiring people leader who creates purpose and clarity, develops strong talent, empowers sound decisions, and enables teams to deliver ambitious outcomes together.
You bring relevant education and professional credibility. An undergraduate or advanced degree in Business, Risk Management, Technology, Finance, or a related field is preferred; relevant risk, audit, technology, product, or project management designations are an asset.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

ICUC is the global leader in Social Media solutions for over 20 years. To date, the ICUC team consists of over 350 people, in over 35 countries, covering 50 languages around the clock. Fueled by a unique culture built in and around meritocracy, we bring the passion, the know-how and the balance necessary to maintain the charted course we set for ourselves: to be the best, we employ the best. Are you ready to be part of the ICUC team?

The Role

ICUC is creating a new leadership role to own our automation and AI strategy across the business. This is a product and innovation mandate, not a workforce-efficiency one: the Director, Product Automation is responsible for how AI and automation get built into the actual work we do for clients — community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening, so our teams can work faster, with more precision, and with sharper focus on the client.

Own ICUC's automation and AI strategy as it applies to our products and service delivery
Evaluate, pilot, and select tools and technologies that make our core services - community management, strategy, insights, monitoring, and social listening - faster, more precise, and more scalable, without compromising the quality clients expect.
Define a standardized, scalable automation blueprint for ICUC's service offerings, rather than one-off, client-by-client fixes.
Build the reporting infrastructure needed to measure automation impact including efficiency gains, quality, and margin — across our platform ecosystem.
Bring a product mindset to this work: treat automation and AI capability as a product to be designed, tested, and iterated, not a back-office project.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner closely with Operations, Product Marketing and Growth to translate our internal automation and AI capability into external go-to-market positioning and messaging.

Work across delivery, operations, and client success teams to ensure new tools and workflows are adopted in practice, not just approved in theory.

Mentor and influence teams across the business to build automation literacy and confidence, without a large direct team of your own at the outset.

Job Description

The Interim Director, Technology GRC will lead and mature governance, risk, and compliance programs across IT and cybersecurity during the interim period. This role oversees IT SOX controls, cybersecurity governance, vendor risk, vulnerability management, and privacy-related technology controls.

The successful candidate will partner with Legal, Technology, Compliance, and business stakeholders to strengthen risk management practices and maintain alignment with regulatory, audit, and policy requirements.

Key Responsibilities

IT SOX Compliance

Oversee the full IT SOX control lifecycle, including annual scoping, testing, remediation, and reporting.
Oversee access management controls, role-based access, and periodic access reviews for in-scope systems while strengthening access governance practices.
Partner with internal teams to ensure SOX controls are properly designed and operating effectively.
Work with internal and external auditors to support efficient audit cycles and timely issue resolution.

Cybersecurity Governance

Develop and maintain cybersecurity policies, risk frameworks, and governance practices aligned with standards such as NIST CSF and ISO 27001.
Track and report enterprise control effectiveness and overall risk posture.
Ensure controls are implemented effectively across on-premises, hybrid, cloud, and SaaS environments.

Vendor Risk Management

Lead third-party risk assessments for technology vendors and service providers.
Partner with procurement and business owners to reduce vendor-related security risks.

Vulnerability Management Oversight

Work with infrastructure and application teams to remediate identified vulnerabilities on time.
Analyze vulnerability data to identify recurring issues and drive lasting improvements.

Privacy and Legal Collaboration

Partner with Legal and Compliance to implement and maintain privacy controls aligned with applicable laws, including GDPR and CCPA.
Coordinate Data Subject Access Requests across technical and business teams to support timely, compliant fulfillment.
Provide risk and control guidance for new initiatives and third-party engagements involving personal or sensitive data.

Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement

Lead cross-functional risk discussions and help stakeholders make informed, risk-aware decisions.
Coach junior team members and help build a strong, accountable GRC culture.
Maintain a clear GRC operating rhythm, including priority tracking, issue follow-up, stakeholder updates, and escalation of key risks or control gaps.
Prepare clear risk, compliance, and control updates for technology leadership, audit stakeholders, and business partners.
Track audit findings, remediation plans, and management action items to ensure issues are resolved on time and supported by appropriate evidence.

Experience

10+ years of experience in IT risk management, audit, cybersecurity governance, compliance, or a related field.
Deep understanding of IT general controls (ITGC), SOX compliance, and technology risk frameworks.
Experience stepping into interim leadership roles with minimal ramp-up time.
Experience managing or contributing to privacy compliance efforts.
Strong background in third-party risk and vulnerability management programs.
Proven ability to work with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business teams.

Education and Designations

Degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Risk Management, or a related field.
Professional certifications such as CISA, CIA, CRISC, or equivalent are strongly preferred.
Familiarity with frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, COBIT, and SOC 2.
